The verdict is pending: nothing fails under either answer to Q11, but two points wait on it. The server windows are defined once, in two module constants in apps/web/convex/lib/lifecycle.ts. HOSPITAL_RETENTION (lines 8-28) holds pre-round 12h, important points 18h, encounter and note 18h, done task 16h, medication, previous note and objective data (vitals, labs, imaging) 36h, and encounter archive 48h. SNF_RETENTION (lines 30-38) holds pre-round 12h, encounter 12h, note 18h, done task 16h, and transcript, previous-note and medication visit counts of 3. hospitalLifecyclePatch and snfLifecyclePatch read every window through these objects. I searched apps/web (convex and src) for hour arithmetic (N * HOUR, 60*60*1000, 12/16/18/36 hours). No other code path keeps its own copy of any window the objects define, so there is no kind-(a) copy. That copy is the only point the oracle fails under either answer to Q11. The windows themselves are compile-time constants with no environment or settings row. That is known gap K9: it passes if Q11 = 'a named constant is enough' and fails if Q11 = 'changeable without a release'. One window is defined only outside the objects (kind b): the client constant NOT_MENTIONED_AFTER_MS = 18h in MedicationsPanel.tsx. It sets when a hospital medication is labelled "not mentioned today" and has no entry in HOSPITAL_RETENTION, so it is pending:Q11 (and on whether a label threshold counts as a retention window). Context only: open tasks and handoffs (36h in…
Product issue (from physicianImpact): To lengthen any retention window (for example under a hospital affiliation), a developer has to edit lifecycle.ts and release new code; an admin cannot change it in settings or the environment. The 18h "not mentioned today" medication label lives separately in the web client, so it needs its own client change and release. / If the Nursing Home previous-notes window were lengthened in the server config, the Previous Notes panel would still stop the physician adding a note at 3 and show "3/3", so the app would not behave the same everywhere. A hospital affiliation's longer windows would also need code changes in several client files, not just one value.

Part (1) passes. DEFAULT_MEDICAL_HINT (apps/web/convex/ai/transcribe.ts:41) is word for word the same as the Whisper prompt string in both prototypes. I ran an exact-string search with the full text, ending at the closing quote, and it found one match in RoundCompanion_aug21b.html (line 6281, formData.append('prompt', ...)) and one in RoundCompanion_PLAYGROUND_p72_HAIKU.html (line 7085). The scripted parity check agrees (verbatim against both). The only thing that differs is the "source :4765" pointer in the code comment: the string sits at line 6281/7085 in these prototype files, not 4765. That is a comment and does not change the hint. Where the hint goes: - **Live path:** prepareSession always sends DEFAULT_MEDICAL_HINT in the realtime transcription session. - **Batch and recovery path:** transcribeAudio sends args.medicalHint || DEFAULT_MEDICAL_HINT. No client call passes medicalHint, so every caller gets the same hospital-oriented hint. The callers are: - Hospital rounding: AddPatient, quick dictation, PreRoundTab, encounter capture, encounter tasks. - Clinic: PreVisitTab, EncounterTab. - Nursing Home (SNF): PreRoundTab, encounter dictation. - The Ask modal. There are no per-surface vocabulary prompts. Whether the hospital vocabulary is right for Nursing Home is Q9 and is outside this verdict. Part (2) waits on the EVALUATION_FRAMEWORK.md copy, which is not under tools/qa-agent/uat/ at this commit.

message:efa12776227e3721e29cc1da607686b7.name:
probes: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue))
Re-checked after review 2026-10-14 (18:00 JST runs: fix-*.json). NH: going offline inside the 800 ms autosave keeps a device copy (one put, no delete); (b) F is restored on the phone and reaches the computer, draft row gone after the echo; (a) the computer's later G wins and F is dropped silently (record-only, Q11). Hospital: the probe (every put/delete on the draft store, init script) shows the copy IS written with a valid key while offline (so the session / draftId is not null) and deleted 4–7 ms later, still offline, while the server never had F; after the page closes F is gone: (b) neither the phone, the computer nor the server has it; (a) G shown, F gone. Cause, from the probe + code: Hospital saves through rounding.update with an optimistic update (src/routes/rounding/Patient.tsx:33) that patches the local chart at once, so useAutosave's 'server echoed my text' check (src/lib/useAutosave.ts:101-110) fires locally and deletes the copy before anything reached the server; Nursing Home saves without one and keeps the copy. That path is local and does not depend on how the network is cut, so it should hold on a real phone in airplane mode — still worth one device check.
Product issue: Hospital pre-round (and every Hospital autosave field that saves through the same optimistic rounding.update): a line typed just before the phone loses signal (within the 0.8 s autosave) is lost if the app is closed before the signal returns — on reopening, the pre-round notes and the computer show nothing of it, while the same flow in Nursing Home restores it. The device copy is written and then deleted at once by the local optimistic echo (Patient.tsx:33 + useAutosave.ts:101-110), before the server has the text. Breaks Empty & Failure States 'nothing typed is lost' (TC-25 S28 b).

All four transcript windows are hard-coded source constants in apps/web/convex/lib/lifecycle.ts, held in two `as const` objects. HOSPITAL_RETENTION (lines 8-28) sets the encounter window to 18 h and the archive window (encounterArchive) to 48 h. SNF_RETENTION (lines 30-38) sets the encounter window to 12 h and transcriptVisits to 3. The lifecycle functions read these constants directly (lines 152, 171, 318, 336-337). I found no environment variable or settings row for retention anywhere in convex/, so lengthening any window means changing the code and deploying it. Against UAT 3.6: the Hospital encounter window (18 h) and the Nursing Home window (12 h) match. The archive window is 48 h, not 36 h, and the visit count is 3, not 2. Every failing point is a recorded gap whose verdict waits on an open question: known:transcript-consts (Q14), known:archive-48h (Q10) and known:visits-3 (Q3). So the verdict is pending, not fail.
